summary: Iteration 6 verification of the rewritten 'Our Global Presence' section. Backend 6/6 pytest pass (regression OK). Structural frontend acceptance criteria ALL PASS: old country cards/grid/testids are fully removed; new map URL contains 'dghkanxm'; [data-testid='world-map'] renders with exactly 5 pins (worldmap-pin-{in,ae,gb,my,sg}); each pin has animated pulse + dot + label; labels read 'United Kingdom','UAE','India · Tap/Hide','Malaysia','Singapore'; clicking worldmap-pin-in toggles india-cities-expand with exactly 16 city chips; clicking again collapses; non-India pins do NOT toggle the expand panel. HOWEVER the #1 user acceptance criterion (pin must land on the correct country) FAILS for ALL 5 pins due to a CSS layout bug. RCA and corrected coordinates are provided below.

ui_bugs.issue: UK pin lands on Greenland / ocean near top edge (y=5.7% of actual image). Should be on British Isles.
India pin lands on Arabian Sea / Oman coast — NOT on Indian subcontinent. This is the user's explicit #1 complaint: 'country ki location aache se dekho wrong hai, indian hai to uspe point karo'.
UAE pin lands on Saudi Arabia / Red Sea (approx 6% too far west).
Malaysia pin lands in Indian Ocean south of India — completely off the SE Asia landmass.
Singapore pin lands deep in Indian Ocean east of Madagascar, nowhere near Singapore.

issues: With .rl-worldmap-inner aspect-ratio 1/1 and object-fit: contain, the 1920x975 map renders as a 1040x528 band centred vertically inside a 1040x1040 box. This leaves ~256px of empty (dark brown) space above and below the map and is the direct cause of the pin miscalibration. Either change the inner container's aspect-ratio to match the image (1920/975) or remap every pin's y value to account for the 24.6% top letterbox.

pin_position_measurements.displayed_image: 1040 x 528 with offsetY=255.9px (object-fit: contain on 1920x975 natural)

ae.note: UAE / Dubai, tip of Arabian peninsula

rca_of_the_issue.symptom: All 5 pins are visibly placed off their target countries on the rendered world map. India pin is the most user-visible offender (floating in Arabian Sea).
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: .rl-worldmap-inner has aspect-ratio: 1/1 but the map PNG is ~1920x975 (≈1.97:1). With object-fit: contain, the rendered picture only fills the middle 528px of the 1040px-tall container — leaving 24.6% empty band above and 24.6% below. Pin coordinates in Footprint.jsx are expressed as a percentage of the CONTAINER, so pins calibrated in image-native space appear shifted vertically toward the top and the x-mapping is also slightly off.
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: 1) Open preview URL, scroll to #footprint. 2) Observe UK pin above Canada/Greenland, Malaysia pin in Indian Ocean, Singapore pin near Australia's meridian in ocean, India pin on the Oman/Arabian Sea coast.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Apply Option A (recommended): in /app/frontend/src/App.css change `.rl-worldmap-inner { aspect-ratio: 1 / 1 }` to `aspect-ratio: 1920 / 975` (or simply `aspect-ratio: 2 / 1`). Then update /app/frontend/src/components/sections/Footprint.jsx `pins` array to the image-native coords listed above. After the fix the India pin will visibly sit on the Indian subcontinent and all 5 countries will be correctly tagged.

critical_code_review_comments: [CRITICAL] Footprint.jsx + App.css coordinate system mismatch: pins positioned in container % but container is letterboxed. Either make container match image aspect-ratio or precompute pin coords in container space. Without this, ANY pin coord appears mis-aligned vertically.

[INFO] The filter `invert(1) sepia(0.35) hue-rotate(355deg) saturate(1.4) brightness(0.92)` on the map is not actually taking effect visibly in preview (map still looks grey/charcoal on brown) — cosmetic only, but worth verifying in a browser that supports the stack.

[MINOR] Malaysia and Singapore pins are only ~2° apart IRL; even at correct coords their labels will visually overlap. Consider offsetting Singapore's label below the dot (top: 14px) instead of above to separate the two pill labels.
